label: <DEL> step (plus original-phase m), content-gated
explanation: Mostly a delimiter-step unit: 71% of activation mass is at the <DEL> step (t == L), where it fires on 8.5% of sequences, and almost never in the copy phase (0.3% of mass, only at recall_idx 1). Most of the remaining mass is original-phase steps that input m (14% of mass, 4% rate), with smaller contributions from 1 and other tokens at mid positions t=4..9. It never fires at t=0 or t=1. Whether it fires at <DEL> depends on sequence content in a distributed way: it is more likely when orig(1) (next_out) is n/u/f/e/c/j, orig(0) is o/u/c/3/n/e, or the last original token is 0/e/w/z. Requiring both the orig(1) and orig(0) conditions raises precision to 0.40 but recall falls to 0.24. Rate rises with to_go during the original phase. The predicate captures about 85% of mass on dev but has low precision (~0.08), because only a minority of <DEL> steps cross threshold and no compact content rule picks them out.
